data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Ammamaria is the goddess of bitterness. She was a nymph who was transformed into a tree after being scorned by a god. Her name is derived from the Greek words 'amma' (mother) and 'mara' (bitterness). The name Ammamaria carries the meaning “Mother of bitterness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ammamaria usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of bitterness and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ammamaria total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
data.cultural_impact: The Christian name "Ammamaria" does not have a significant cultural impact as it does not have a historical or traditional association with the Christian faith. Furthermore, there is no recorded usage of this name within Christianity.
data.spiritual_significance: However, spiritually, the name "Ammamaria" carries a profound meaning for those who choose it as their given name. The Greek roots of the name 'amma' (mother) and 'mara' (bitterness) can be interpreted as a reminder of the bitterness and sorrow that mothers may experience in the course of raising their children. It can also serve as a reminder of the bitterness and sorrow that comes with the human condition and the importance of seeking comfort and consolation in God during difficult times.
